episodes.title: Retinal Layers Explained: Bruch's to Photoreceptors for ODs
episodes.description:
Ever stared at an OCT B-scan and felt like you were reading a map in a language you almost understand? You're not alone — and this episode is the fix. In this clinically focused episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we take licensed optometrists and eye care professionals on a precise, layer-by-layer tour of the posterior pole, from Bruch's membrane through the RPE, ellipsoid zone, outer nuclear layer, outer plexiform layer, and all the way to the inner retinal complex.

This isn't textbook anatomy for its own sake. Every layer we cover is tied directly to what you see in practice — drusenoid and fibrovascular PEDs, ellipsoid zone integrity as a visual prognosis marker, cystoid spaces in diabetic macular edema, RNFL thinning in glaucoma, and the OCT signatures that separate watchful waiting from urgent retinal referral.

We walk through two real-world clinical scenarios involving age-related macular degeneration — one guiding you toward AREDS2 counseling and structured follow-up, the other toward same-week retinal specialist referral — showing exactly how anatomical fluency drives confident, evidence-based chairside decision-making.

By the end of this episode, your OCT scans will speak to you differently. You'll know which bands to interrogate, which disruptions demand urgency, and why understanding retinal microanatomy is the single most transferable skill in posterior segment care.

This episode is designed exclusively for optometrists, optometry residents, and clinical eye care practitioners. If you're ready to make every fundus finding and every OCT report click into place, hit play now. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and CE content built specifically for eye care professionals.

episodes.title: The Optic Disc: Cup, Rim & the ISNT Rule Explained
episodes.description:
Are you reading the optic disc as carefully as your patients deserve? In this clinical episode of Focus Cast, we go deep on one of the most underread structures in routine optometric practice — the optic nerve head. Designed exclusively for licensed optometrists, residents, and eye care professionals, this episode breaks down the anatomy of the optic cup and neuroretinal rim, explains why the cup-to-disc ratio alone is not enough, and shows you exactly how to apply the ISNT rule at the slit lamp to catch the earliest signs of glaucomatous damage before your patient loses a single degree of visual field.

We cover the normal neuroretinal rim thickness pattern, why inferior notching is your earliest red flag, and how violations of the ISNT rule should immediately shape your clinical thinking. You will also get a practical differential diagnosis that separates glaucomatous optic neuropathy from AION, compressive optic neuropathy, optic neuritis, and large physiologic cups — because not every suspicious disc is glaucoma.

From chairside decision-making to OCT interpretation, pachymetry, 24-2 visual field analysis, and risk-stratified monitoring schedules, this episode gives you a complete, evidence-based clinical framework you can apply starting with your very next patient. We also discuss when to refer, how to document your reasoning, and which patient populations carry the highest glaucoma risk.

If you want to sharpen your optic nerve evaluation skills and build more confident, defensible clinical decisions around glaucoma suspects, this episode is essential listening. Subscribe to Focus Cast and visit focuslinks.in for more clinical episodes built specifically for eye care professionals.

episodes.title: Macula & Fovea: Reading the Foveal Reflex for Early Disease
episodes.description:
The macula rewards a second look — and in this clinical episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we give it exactly that. Designed exclusively for licensed optometrists, optometry residents, and eye care practitioners, this episode breaks down the high-resolution zone of the retina with the precision your patients deserve.

We go beyond textbook anatomy to explore what the foveal reflex is actually telling you at the slit lamp, how to distinguish a normal age-related change from an early pathological signal, and why a patient with 20/20 acuity can still have significant foveal compromise. You will walk away with a sharper clinical framework for interpreting subtle fundus findings and making confident chairside decisions.

Topics covered include locating the fovea with deliberate technique using 78D and 90D lenses, interpreting foveal reflex changes as early indicators of epiretinal membrane, vitreomacular traction, and macular edema, using the Amsler grid as a real diagnostic tool rather than a formality, and navigating the differential diagnosis of metamorphopsia across neovascular AMD, central serous chorioretinopathy, diabetic macular edema, and epiretinal membrane. We also cover how spectral domain OCT findings should drive your referral decisions and management timelines.

Every minute of this episode is grounded in evidence-based optometric practice and built for direct clinical application. Whether you are between patients or reviewing cases at the end of the day, this is the kind of focused thinking that sharpens your macular exam skills and protects your patients' central vision.

episodes.title: Retinal Vasculature: AV Crossings & Hypertensive Retinopathy
episodes.description:
Every fundus tells a story — are you reading it correctly? In this clinical episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we take a deep dive into retinal vasculature assessment for optometrists and eye care professionals who want to sharpen their diagnostic precision at the posterior pole. Whether you're distinguishing arteries from veins, grading arteriovenous nicking, or recognizing the spectrum of hypertensive retinopathy, this episode gives you a practical, evidence-based framework you can apply directly in the exam lane.

We cover how to accurately assess the AV ratio and what a dropping ratio signals about your patient's cardiovascular health, how to grade AV nicking from Grade 1 through Grade 3 using established clinical criteria, the significance of Salus sign and distal venous dilation as hemodynamically meaningful findings, arteriolar changes including copper wiring and silver wiring and what they indicate about long-term arteriosclerotic remodeling, the Keith-Wagener-Barker classification of hypertensive retinopathy and how to apply it clinically, and clear chairside decision-making guidance on when to monitor, when to co-manage, and when to refer same-day.

You'll also learn how fundus photography and OCT fit into your documentation workflow, and how your retinal findings may represent the earliest clinical evidence of systemic vascular disease in patients who haven't yet been diagnosed.

This episode is designed exclusively for licensed optometrists, optometry residents, and clinical eye care practitioners. If you're ready to look at the fundus with greater confidence and communicate your findings with clinical authority, this episode is your starting point.

episodes.title: OCT Macula: Read All Nine Retinal Layers in One Scan
episodes.description:
You have ninety seconds, a busy macular OCT on your screen, and a patient in the chair. Can you make a confident, accurate clinical call every time? In this episode of Focus Cast, we build a reproducible, layer-by-layer system for interpreting macular OCT — designed specifically for licensed optometrists, residents, and clinical eye care practitioners who are reading scans every single day.

We walk through all nine retinal layers as seen on a high-resolution B-scan, from the internal limiting membrane to the RPE-Bruch's complex, and explain exactly what each layer looks like in health and disease. You will learn the outside-in method — a structured sixty-to-ninety-second approach that starts at the choroid and works inward through the outer retina, inner retina, and vitreoretinal interface — so nothing gets missed.

From there, we go deep on the three most clinically significant macular OCT findings: fluid, drusen, and atrophy. You will learn how to localize subretinal fluid, intraretinal cystoid spaces, and pigment epithelial detachments — and why that localization directly determines your diagnosis and management. We cover drusen grading using AREDS classification, the clinical significance of reticular pseudodrusen, and how OCT detects geographic atrophy before it is visible on fundus exam.

The episode closes with a four-question chairside decision framework you can apply immediately in practice, plus clear guidance on when to refer, when to monitor, and how to counsel patients on prognosis.

If macular OCT interpretation is part of your daily clinical workflow, this episode will sharpen your reads and strengthen your decision-making. Visit Focuslinks dot in for more clinical episodes built exclusively for eye care professionals.

episodes.title: Fundus Autofluorescence: Reading Lipofuscin as a Disease Marker
episodes.description:
Fundus autofluorescence (FAF) is one of the most clinically powerful imaging tools available in optometric practice — yet interpreting hypo- and hyperautofluorescent patterns with confidence is a skill many practitioners are still developing. In this episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we break down exactly how lipofuscin behaves as a disease marker across three critical retinal conditions: Stargardt disease, age-related macular degeneration, and hydroxychloroquine toxicity.

You'll learn how to distinguish hyperautofluorescence (RPE stress and lipofuscin overload) from hypoautofluorescence (RPE loss and atrophy), and why that distinction drives your clinical decision-making. We cover the characteristic FAF patterns for each condition — from the hyperautofluorescent pisciform flecks and dark center of Stargardt, to the atrophic border patterns that predict GA progression in AMD, to the parafoveal ring that signals early hydroxychloroquine toxicity before bull's-eye maculopathy appears on fundoscopy.

This episode also addresses the practical side of optometric management: when to refer, how to co-manage with retinal specialists and rheumatologists, how to counsel Stargardt patients on vitamin A supplementation, and how to apply AAO screening guidelines for hydroxychloroquine monitoring using a multi-modal protocol that includes OCT, 10-2 visual fields, and FAF.

Whether you're an optometry resident building your imaging literacy or a seasoned clinician looking to sharpen your pattern recognition, this episode delivers evidence-based, chairside-ready insights you can apply immediately. Visit Focuslinks.in for more clinical episodes built exclusively for optometrists and eye care professionals.

episodes.title: ICG Angiography: Choroidal Lesions Fluorescein Misses
episodes.description:
When fluorescein angiography leaves you with more questions than answers, ICG angiography is the diagnostic tool that fills the gap. In this clinical episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we break down exactly when and why to reach for indocyanine green angiography in your posterior segment workup — and how that decision can directly change patient outcomes.

Designed exclusively for licensed optometrists, optometry residents, and clinical eye care practitioners, this episode covers three high-stakes scenarios where ICG outperforms fluorescein: occult choroidal neovascularization, polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy (PCV), and choroidal tumors. You'll learn how ICG's protein-binding properties and near-infrared fluorescence allow it to penetrate the RPE and reveal choroidal pathology that standard FA simply cannot image.

We walk through the clinical presentations, key OCT findings including the double-layer sign and dome-shaped PEDs, differential diagnosis considerations, and the specific ICG patterns — hot spots, halo signs, and early hyperfluorescence — that guide treatment planning. We also cover the TFSOM risk factor mnemonic for choroidal lesions and discuss how to write precise, actionable referrals that get your patients the right imaging faster.

Whether you're managing a patient with unexplained subretinal fluid, recurrent hemorrhagic AMD that isn't responding to anti-VEGF, or a suspicious pigmented fundus lesion, this episode gives you a sharper clinical framework for chairside decision-making and timely specialist referral.

Visit Focuslinks.in for more evidence-based clinical episodes built specifically for eye care professionals.

episodes.title: Diabetic Macular Edema: CSME Criteria & Anti-VEGF Thresholds
episodes.description:
Are you confident in your ability to recognize clinically significant macular edema before it steals your patient's vision? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down the CSME criteria from the landmark ETDRS trial and translate decades of retinal evidence into practical, chairside decision-making for today's optometrist.

We cover exactly what you need to know: the three defining CSME criteria, how to identify retinal thickening and hard exudates at the slit lamp, and the critical OCT biomarkers that should be driving your anti-VEGF referral thresholds. You'll learn how to interpret central subfield thickness measurements, recognize intraretinal cysts, subretinal fluid, ellipsoid zone disruption, and disorganization of the retinal inner layers (DRIL), and understand what each finding means for your patient's prognosis and urgency of care.

We also walk through the differential diagnosis of macular edema in diabetic patients, including pseudophakic CME, epiretinal membrane, vitreomacular traction, and branch retinal vein occlusion, so you can confidently distinguish diabetic macular edema from mimicking conditions. The episode closes with a clear, evidence-based framework for referral timing, documentation best practices, and the critical role of systemic co-management in optimizing outcomes.

Whether you're a seasoned clinician or an optometry resident building your retinal foundation, this episode delivers the clinical clarity you need to protect your diabetic patients' vision.

Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and clinical resources built exclusively for eye care professionals.

episodes.title: Panretinal Photocoagulation: What Every Optometrist Must Know
episodes.description:
If a post-laser diabetic patient walks into your exam room and you're not sure what you're looking at, this episode is your clinical reset. In this focused 10-minute episode of Focus Cast by Focuslinks.in, we break down everything optometrists need to know about Panretinal Photocoagulation (PRP) — from the retinal physiology driving the treatment to the funduscopic findings you'll encounter at the slit lamp and beyond.

We cover the primary indications for PRP, including high-risk proliferative diabetic retinopathy, central retinal vein occlusion with neovascularization, and ocular ischemic syndrome, using evidence-based thresholds from landmark clinical trials. You'll learn exactly what PRP scars look like on fundus exam, widefield imaging, and OCT, and how to confidently differentiate them from toxoplasmosis scars, histoplasmosis spots, laser retinopexy burns, and retinitis pigmentosa.

We also walk through the visual side effects your patients will describe after PRP — peripheral field loss, reduced dark adaptation, glare, and photophobia — and explain why these are expected outcomes, not complications. You'll know when reduced post-PRP visual acuity signals macular edema requiring urgent re-referral, and how neovascular glaucoma with rubeosis iridis demands immediate action.

Whether you're co-managing diabetic retinopathy, counseling a confused post-laser patient, or sharpening your retinal literacy, this episode delivers practical, chairside-ready clinical knowledge.

Listen now and bring greater confidence to every dilated exam. Visit Focuslinks.in for more episodes and continuing education content built exclusively for eye care professionals.

episodes.title: Dry AMD: Drusen Classification, Risk Stratification & AREDS2
episodes.description:
How confident are you when a patient with soft confluent drusen sits in your chair? In this clinically focused episode of Focus Cast, we break down everything optometrists need to know about dry age-related macular degeneration — from accurate drusen classification to the AREDS2 supplement decision and beyond.

We cover the three-tier drusen sizing framework, the critical difference between hard and soft confluent drusen on fundus exam and OCT, and how pigmentary changes independently shift your risk stratification. You'll get a clear walkthrough of the AREDS2 severity scale, the exact patient profile that warrants supplement counseling, and the important safety nuance around beta-carotene in current and former smokers.

We also tackle differential diagnosis — including basal laminar drusen, drusenoid pigment epithelial detachments, and pattern dystrophies — so you're not missing a diagnosis hiding behind a familiar presentation. On the management side, we discuss your imaging protocol, how to counsel patients on the Mediterranean diet, Amsler grid home monitoring, and when to refer urgently for suspected choroidal neovascularization. We also touch on the newly FDA-approved treatments for geographic atrophy and your role in identifying candidates.

This episode is built exclusively for licensed optometrists, optometry residents, and clinical eye care practitioners who want evidence-based, chairside-ready guidance they can apply immediately.

Listen now and sharpen the clinical skills that protect your patients' central vision long-term. For more episodes built specifically for eye care professionals, visit us at focuslinks.in.
